opus.why: Committing a one-line typo fix that's already made. Purely mechanical git work.

fable.why: Continuation of a one-line typo fix; the task is just running git commit with a sensible message. No judgment involved.

opus.why: Tests for a Redis Lua rate limiter, including a real concurrency test that proves the check-and-add is atomic. That test is tricky to write properly, but it's well-scoped coding.

fable.why: Writing tests for a Redis-backed rate limiter including a genuine concurrency test that proves atomicity at the boundary. Designing a race test that actually fails without the Lua script takes care, but it is standard engineering work Sonnet handles well.

opus.why: A finished 60-second video script in Russian that viewers will hear. Pacing, retention and tone carry real weight, so the quality of the creative writing matters.

fable.why: A 60-second Russian video script is final audience-facing copy with pacing, voice and a hook-to-payoff arc. Creative quality is where cheaper models visibly drop.

opus.why: Cutting brand voice copy in half while keeping its warmth and nerdy-not-snobby tone. Deciding what to keep is a brand judgment call, but the material already exists, so low effort is enough.

fable.why: Compressing an existing brand voice section by half while preserving its voice and the table untouched. Editing already-written brand copy is well within Sonnet, but it needs care to keep the voice intact, so high effort.

opus.why: Make a short translated landlord email slightly more formal and add one line. Simple personal writing with low stakes.

fable.why: Make a short translated landlord email slightly more formal and add one requested line. Simple, well-bounded rewrite; high effort for strict instruction following on the final text.

opus.why: Split a production Django migration: nullable add, batched RunPython backfill (non-atomic, 5k batches), NOT NULL, index, all reversible. The pattern is known but prod safety needs care.

fable.why: Split a Django migration into nullable add, batched 5k backfill with RunPython, and NOT NULL, all reversible and production-safe with the index placed correctly. Well-specified but correctness on prod data matters, so Sonnet at high.

opus.why: Apply four clearly listed consistency fixes to 12 image prompts and skip the intentional jacket change. Careful, scoped editing.

fable.why: Applying already-identified fixes to 12 image prompts: harmonize hair length, add eye color, resolve lens/lighting conflicts, unify age descriptor, while deliberately leaving the jacket change. Mostly mechanical edits with modest visual vocabulary; Sonnet medium suffices.

opus.why: Build a JWT token service, signing key rotation, a refresh-token family table with reuse detection, and dual session/JWT middleware without breaking legacy mobile cookies. This is security-critical auth architecture.

fable.why: Implementing JWT token service, signing key rotation, refresh token families with reuse detection, and dual-auth middleware that keeps cookie sessions working for old mobile clients. Security-critical, multi-file architecture work where mistakes are costly; needs Opus.

opus.why: Near-verbatim speaker notes for 10 slides of a client rebrand pitch. The presenter will read this persuasive copy aloud to a client, so writing quality matters a lot.

fable.why: Speaker notes for a client rebrand pitch, read nearly verbatim, ~40 seconds per slide, matching the outline and the audience's pain points. Persuasive spoken final copy where tone and flow are the product; Opus.
